planApproval.note: Graduated 'required' -> 'auto' by the user, 2026-08-01 (see review-feedback: review-gate-graduation). /plan-issue posts the plan and proceeds to /execute, EXCEPT: plans for issues carrying any label in alwaysRequiredFor STILL stop for user approval — ADRs are major decisions and the user steers at this altitude — and any plan whose Risks section contains a question only the user can answer stops and surfaces it.
planApproval.debtBurn: Issues labelled 'debt-burn' skip plan approval: the issue body IS the plan (triage only applies the label to small, proven, well-scoped work with named files and mechanical acceptance). Anything needing a re-structure or re-think is not labelled debt-burn and keeps the full gates.

merge.autoRule: A PR auto-merges once CI is green iff it contains NO source-code files AND touches nothing under humanAlways paths. Source code = extensions .ts .tsx .js .mjs .cjs .sh .py .tf .sql — files whose structure (functions, modules, components) the user reviews. Markdown, JSON, YAML, and other plain config auto-merge.
merge.reviewedSourceRule: A source-code PR auto-merges once CI is green AND the review loop ended in APPROVE, unless it touches a humanAlways path. Graduated by the user 2026-08-01 (see review-feedback: review-gate-graduation) — the generalisation of debtBurnRule and refactorRule after every source PR this stretch (#95 #97 #114 #116 #119 #121 #124 #130 #131 #132) merged on exactly that evidence. The review loop's APPROVE is the load-bearing gate: no APPROVE, no merge, regardless of CI.
merge.humanAlwaysRule: PRs touching a humanAlways path: CI green, then label 'awaiting-review', notify the user with a short review guide, do NOT merge (chat approval from the user also unblocks); continue with independent tickets while it waits. ADRs decide direction; workflow.json and CLAUDE.md ARE the gates — they never pass through the gates they define.
merge.mergeRitual: A PR that carries 'awaiting-review' logs its own review-feedback line ON THE BRANCH, before it merges: the docs/review-feedback.md entry (category from the closed vocabulary, even when the verdict is just 'approved, no changes') is part of the diff the owner approves, added in the commit that responds to the approval. At merge the only remaining step is taking the label off. Moved from after-merge to on-branch 2026-08-10 after PR #345 omitted the line while its body claimed it, and PR #348 deferred its own line to a later PR — a step owed after the merge is a step no gate can block. A quiet feedback category must be distinguishable from an unlogged one, or nothing can ever graduate; this ritual is what made reviewedSourceRule graduatable.
merge.mergeRitualGate: Mechanical half: a CI check fails any PR labelled 'awaiting-review' whose diff does not touch docs/review-feedback.md. Wire it into .github/workflows/ci.yml as its own job (not into `pnpm verify`, which knows nothing about labels). The check is a floor, not a proof — it cannot tell a good entry from a placeholder — which is why the prose half above still owns what the entry must say.
merge.debtBurnRule: A PR closing a 'debt-burn'-labelled issue auto-merges once CI is green AND the review loop ended in APPROVE, even when it touches source code. Decided by the user 2026-07-30 (see review-feedback: debt-burn-lane). Subsumed by reviewedSourceRule 2026-08-01 but kept as the planApproval half's anchor: debt-burn also skips plan approval.
merge.note: Further relaxation (or tightening after a bad merge) is proposed via retro PR — the user decides. A merge later shown to be wrong reverts via a plain revert PR and gets a review-feedback entry naming what the review loop missed.

orchestration.note: flat = top-level runs plan-issue/execute/review-loop inline; delegated-pilot = /run-issue on selected issues while the owner evaluates; delegated = default. Graduation/rollback criteria live in the proposing retro PR. The top-level session owns merging in every mode.
